Physical activity and sleep quality in older adults: a cross-sectional study

Background: Poor sleep is common in older adults. Aims: To estimate the association between physical activity and sleep quality in community-dwelling older adults. Methods: Cross-sectional study with 312 participants aged 60 or more, who answered the IPAQ and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Logistic regression was adjusted for age, sex and depression. Findings: Active participants had lower odds of poor sleep (OR = 0.58; 95% CI 0.36–0.93; p = 0.02). Conclusions: Physical activity is associated with better sleep in older adults.
Keywords: aging; sleep; exercise.
